lessons.title: Gold as a store of value
lessons.summary: Why people have trusted gold for thousands of years — and its limits.

cards.title: Holds value
cards.body: Gold can't be printed, rarely rusts or breaks, and is wanted worldwide. Over long periods it has tended to keep its buying power.

cards.title: No income
cards.body: Gold pays no interest and no dividends. Your return comes only from the price going up — which it doesn't always do.

cards.title: 24K vs 22K
cards.body: 24K is 99.9% pure, used for bullion (bars and coins). 22K is 91.6% gold mixed with other metals, which makes it harder — used for jewellery.

quiz.question: What income does gold pay while you hold it?
quiz.explanation: Your return depends only on its price.

quiz.question: Why is 22K used for jewellery?
options: The mixed metals make it harder and more durable

lessons.title: Grams and sovereigns
lessons.summary: How gold is priced in Sri Lanka.

cards.title: Per gram
cards.body: Prices are quoted per gram. The trainer starts from the same reference price shown on your Home screen's "Market today" card.

cards.title: The sovereign (pavun)
cards.body: Jewellers often quote per sovereign — 8 grams. If gold is Rs 25,000 a gram, a sovereign of 24K is Rs 200,000.

cards.title: 22K pricing
cards.body: A gram of 22K contains 0.916 g of pure gold, so it's priced at about 91.6% of 24K.

quiz.question: How many grams in one sovereign?
24K gold is Rs 25,000/g. About how much is 1 g of 22K?
Where does the trainer's starting gold price come from?
options: The same reference as Home's Market today card
quiz.explanation: They start from the same source, so the numbers match.

lessons.title: The spread and making charges
lessons.summary: The hidden costs of buying gold.

cards.title: Buy high, sell low
cards.body: Dealers sell to you above the market price and buy back below it. That gap is the spread. In the trainer it's 3% in total.

cards.title: Making charges
cards.body: Jewellery adds a making charge for the craftsmanship — often 10–20%. When you sell jewellery, you're paid only for the gold weight, so the making charge is gone.

cards.title: Bullion for investing
cards.body: If your goal is investment, bullion avoids making charges. Jewellery is something you enjoy wearing; treat it as consumption, not an investment.

quiz.question: The spread is…
options: The gap between the buying and selling price

quiz.question: When you sell gold jewellery, the making charge is…
quiz.explanation: You're paid for the gold content only.

quiz.question: You buy and immediately sell gold. What happens?
quiz.explanation: The price must rise more than the spread before you profit.

cards.title: Priced in dollars
cards.body: Gold trades worldwide in US dollars. The Sri Lankan price is roughly the dollar price × the USD/LKR rate.

cards.title: Rupee moves matter
cards.body: If the rupee weakens against the dollar, local gold prices rise even if the world price doesn't change.

cards.title: Inflation hedge
cards.body: When people worry about inflation or crises, they buy gold, pushing prices up. This 'hedge' works over long periods, but not every year.

cards.title: Global demand
cards.body: Central banks, jewellery demand in India and China, and investors all move the price. When shares look exciting, gold can fall.

quiz.question: The rupee weakens against the dollar. What usually happens to local gold prices?
quiz.explanation: Each dollar of gold now costs more rupees.

quiz.question: Gold as an 'inflation hedge' means…
options: It always beats inflation every year
It has tended to hold value when prices rise over long periods
It pays interest linked to inflation
quiz.explanation: It's a long-run tendency, not a guarantee.

quiz.question: Gold's world price is mainly quoted in…
quiz.explanation: Local prices are converted from the dollar price.
